scopeNote: Whole-internet scope per FORGE.md creative mandate. New batches must be category-diverse with at most 1 local/agency-adjacent idea. SHIPPED so far: ShipSafe, LeakCheck, ExposureCheck (the 'ship-safety suite' — they cross-promote). The 5 parked ideas are the old narrow local set, kept for revival but off the active pick-list.

ideas.title: ExposureCheck — is your live site leaking?
ideas.oneliner: Enter your deployed URL (or paste your built bundle) and see what a public visitor can already grab: exposed .env/.git/config files, secrets hardcoded in your JS bundle, leaked source maps, and internal endpoints.
ideas.problem: Vibe-coded and rushed deploys routinely ship .env files, public .git folders, source maps, and hardcoded API keys to production where anyone can fetch them. Builders never check, and the existing tools (nuclei, gitleaks on the server, security scanners) are dev-ops/pentest tools non-experts won't run.
ideas.who: Indie devs, no-code/vibe builders, and small teams who deployed fast — the same audience as ShipSafe + LeakCheck. Global.
ideas.gap: Server-side / pentest scanners exist but are technical and dev-ops-facing; there's no instant, plain-English, no-signup web tool that checks a DEPLOYED site for leaked secrets/files/source and explains the fix to a non-expert. The wedge is framing + being the deployed-site sibling to LeakCheck.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page, client-side. URL mode fetches the page + same-origin scripts via a public CORS-proxy fallback chain and probes ~12 sensitive paths; paste mode (always works) analyzes a pasted bundle. Reuses LeakCheck's detectors + masking + design. ~2-3 day build, zero-secret. Paid later: scheduled re-scans + CI ruleset pack (shared with LeakCheck).
ideas.notes: SHIPPED 2026-06-08 — product #4, completes the ship-safety suite (ShipSafe=sued / LeakCheck=code secrets / ExposureCheck=live site); the three cross-link to compound traffic. Forked LeakCheck (detectors + design) via a 7-agent swarm, 0 blockers. Independently verified: XSS-safe vs fetched content (no innerHTML; textContent only), secrets masked (live test: 16 exposures, no raw secret in DOM), defensive 'scan your own site' framing. Known limit: URL mode depends on public CORS proxies (paste mode is the reliable path); security-headers check is informational only. See builds/exposurecheck.md.

ideas.title: LeakCheck — paste-and-scan secret detector
ideas.oneliner: Paste a code snippet, .env, or config and instantly see exposed API keys, tokens, and private keys flagged by severity — 100% in your browser, nothing uploaded.
ideas.problem: Hardcoded secrets are the #1 way indie and AI-assisted projects get popped — keys committed to public repos, pasted into Discord, shipped in client bundles. Existing scanners (gitleaks, trufflehog) are CLI/dev-ops tools nobody outside security runs, and pasting code into a random website to 'check it' is itself the risk.
ideas.who: The whole developer internet, especially the explosion of vibe-coders / no-code builders (same audience ShipSafe already reaches), plus students and bootcamp grads.
ideas.gap: All credible scanners are CLI or CI-pipeline tools; there is no trustworthy, instant, plain-English web tool that runs entirely client-side (provably no upload) and explains WHICH secret, WHY it's dangerous, and HOW to rotate it. The wedge is zero-trust (client-side) + plain-English remediation.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page; a regex/entropy ruleset (AWS, Stripe, OpenAI, GitHub, JWT, private keys, etc.) runs in-browser with a visible 'nothing leaves this tab' guarantee. Output: severity-ranked findings + per-type rotation steps. ~2-day build, zero-secret. Paid later: downloadable pre-commit ruleset / org policy pack.
ideas.notes: SHIPPED 2026-06-08 — product #3 and the FIRST under the widened-scope mandate. Built by a 7-agent forge swarm. Security promise independently verified: zero network on user data, XSS-safe, secrets always masked. Gotcha: GitHub push protection blocked the demo's Stripe test key — fixed by fragmenting example secrets at runtime. Forked by ExposureCheck. See builds/leakcheck.md.

ideas.title: TrueRate — what to actually charge
ideas.oneliner: Enter your target take-home, real billable hours, expenses, and tax rate, and get the hourly/day rate you must charge to hit it — with every assumption shown.
ideas.problem: Freelancers and indie consultants chronically underprice because they price off a salary number and forget non-billable time, expenses, downtime, and self-employment tax. The result is working full-time and netting part-time.
ideas.who: The global freelance / contractor / solopreneur workforce (tens of millions, growing) — designers, devs, writers, coaches, trades-for-themselves.
ideas.gap: Most 'freelance rate calculators' are thin blog lead-magnets that gloss over tax and utilization. A transparent, shareable, genuinely-does-the-math tool (billable-hour utilization + expense load + tax gross-up) with a copyable breakdown is underserved.
ideas.buildPlan: Static client-side calculator; inputs -> required rate with a labeled waterfall. Copy/Share + shareable URL encoding the scenario. ~1-2 day build, zero-secret. Paid later: country tax presets, invoice export.
ideas.notes: Evergreen high-intent SEO. Honest-by-construction with a broad global audience. No regulated advice — pure arithmetic. Owner found it weak in 2026-06-08 review; deprioritized in favor of the dev 'ship-safety' suite.

ideas.title: Caffeine Curve — see the coffee in your system
ideas.oneliner: Log your coffees and energy drinks and watch a live curve of how much caffeine is in your bloodstream right now, plus when it'll drop below a sleep-safe level.
ideas.problem: People feel wired at 11pm and don't connect it to the 3pm latte. Caffeine has a ~5-6h half-life, so an afternoon dose is still ~half-strength at bedtime — but nobody does that math.
ideas.who: Basically everyone who drinks caffeine and cares about sleep — a massive, global, relatable audience.
ideas.gap: There are static 'half-life' blog explainers and a couple of clunky apps, but no clean, instant, no-signup web tool that plots YOUR intake as a live decay curve and tells you a concrete 'safe to sleep by' time.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page; add drinks at times -> superposed exponential-decay curve + 'below 50mg by HH:MM'. Published pharmacokinetics, NOT medical advice (disclaimer). ~1-2 day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: Viral/shareable with strong evergreen SEO. Guardrail-safe: documented decay model + disclaimers, no health claims. Owner found it weak in 2026-06-08 review; deprioritized in favor of the dev 'ship-safety' suite.

ideas.title: SubAudit — your subscription reality check
ideas.oneliner: Add your subscriptions once and see your true annual spend, a renewal calendar you can export, and a ranked 'cancel these first' list by cost-per-use.
ideas.problem: Subscription creep is a near-universal money leak — people genuinely don't know their monthly burn or when things renew, and surprise annual charges hit because nothing reminds them.
ideas.who: Global consumers drowning in SaaS/streaming/app subscriptions — an enormous, evergreen audience.
ideas.gap: The 'automatic' subscription managers demand bank-account access, which most people won't grant for a quick gut-check. A privacy-first, no-login, manual tool that stays in the browser fills the trust gap.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page; localStorage list -> annualized total, per-use cost, next-renewal timeline, .ics export. ~2-day build, zero-secret. Paid later: cloud sync.
ideas.notes: Privacy-first (no bank link) is the wedge AND the marketing angle. Strong SEO and a shareable 'I was paying $X/yr' moment.

ideas.title: DeckShare — flashcards in a link
ideas.oneliner: Make a flashcard deck in your browser, study it with spaced repetition, and share the whole deck as a single URL — no account, no app install.
ideas.problem: Anki is powerful but intimidating and install-heavy; Quizlet has paywalled study modes and aggressive monetization. Students just want to make a deck and send it to a study group in one click.
ideas.who: Students, language learners, and self-learners worldwide — a huge, perennial, globally-distributed audience.
ideas.gap: The friction-free middle is open: a free, no-login, genuinely-shareable deck with real spaced-repetition and zero paywall. Every shared deck is a viral seed.
ideas.buildPlan: Static SPA; SM-2 spaced repetition in localStorage, shareable deck URL or static publish. ~3-day build, zero-secret. Paid later: cloud decks, class accounts.
ideas.notes: Built-in word-of-mouth loop: every shared deck markets the tool. Public decks compound into an SEO content moat.

ideas.title: FrostPlan — when to plant, for your zip
ideas.oneliner: Enter your location and get your last/first frost dates plus a personalized seed-starting and planting calendar you can export as reminders.
ideas.problem: New gardeners kill plants by sowing too early or transplanting before the last frost. The frost-date + count-back-the-weeks math is annoying and scattered across extension-service PDFs.
ideas.who: The huge, global home-gardening hobby audience — and it spikes hard every spring (seasonal SEO goldmine).
ideas.gap: Frost-date lookups exist but are ugly, ad-choked, and stop at the date. A clean tool that turns the date into a personalized planting schedule with reminders is underserved.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page; bundled frost-date dataset + per-crop weeks-before/after table -> personalized calendar + .ics export. ~2-3 day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: Massive evergreen + seasonal SEO. Content moat: per-crop/per-region pages scale to thousands of long-tail landing pages.

ideas.title: RacePace — splits and goal times
ideas.oneliner: Enter a goal race time and get your exact per-mile/km splits, pace bands, and predicted finish times at every other distance.
ideas.problem: Runners training for a race need to know their target splits and what a recent time predicts for a longer race, but end up juggling spreadsheets or paywalled apps.
ideas.who: The global running and endurance community — millions training for 5Ks to marathons year-round.
ideas.gap: Plenty of bare pace calculators exist, but few combine a clean split table + race-equivalency prediction + a shareable race-day pace band in one polished, no-signup tool.
ideas.buildPlan: Static calculator; goal time -> splits, pace bands, equivalent times via published formulas. Printable race-day band. ~1-2 day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: Evergreen SEO. Printable pace band is a race-day virality hook. Lower defensibility (public formulas) — win on polish + all-in-one.

ideas.title: PaletteForge — accessible color palettes
ideas.oneliner: Generate harmonious color palettes and gradients, check every pair for WCAG contrast, and export straight to Tailwind, CSS variables, or SVG.
ideas.problem: Designers and (especially) developers waste time hand-tuning palettes and then ship inaccessible color combos that fail contrast checks. Existing generators rarely bake accessibility in or export to the formats devs actually paste.
ideas.who: The global design + front-end developer community — a large, high-intent, share-happy audience.
ideas.gap: Color tools are fragmented: pretty generators ignore accessibility; contrast checkers ignore generation; few export clean Tailwind/CSS tokens. The integrated flow is the wedge.
ideas.buildPlan: Static SPA; palette/gradient gen, live WCAG contrast grid, export to Tailwind/CSS vars/SVG/JSON. Shareable URL. ~2-day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: Crowded space (Coolors etc.) so scored at threshold — only ship if we win on accessibility-first + dev-export. Lowest-priority; included for breadth.

ideas.title: Vibe-Coded App Health Checker
ideas.oneliner: Paste a URL and get a plain-English report on ADA/WCAG gaps, missing privacy policy/cookie banner, broken schema, and demand-letter risk.
ideas.problem: Lovable/Bolt/v0/Cursor produced an explosion of apps from non-devs who ship zero WCAG compliance (4,600+ ADA suits in 2024), no privacy policy, and broken ARIA. They don't find out until a demand letter arrives.
ideas.who: Hundreds of thousands of indie / no-code builders shipping AI-generated sites; Copper Bay's own client-site audits; Boots students.
ideas.gap: WAVE/axe/Lighthouse all exist and are free, but NONE combine accessibility + privacy-policy detection + schema validation + plain-English demand-letter risk framing in one non-technical report. The wedge is framing + combined output.
ideas.buildPlan: Serverless/proxy fetch wraps accessibility + privacy + schema checks. Plain-English risk report card. Paid tier: scheduled re-checks.
ideas.notes: Product #1, shipped. Anchor of the 'ship-safety suite' (legal/accessibility leg). Broad global dev audience. Perfect ProductHunt/Discord/dev-SEO fit.

ideas.title: ReserveRight (Winery & Charter edition)
ideas.oneliner: A drop-in deposit-and-hold widget that collects a Stripe deposit and sends reminder texts for wine tastings, tours, and fishing/kayak charters — no platform migration.
ideas.problem: No-shows destroy revenue on time-boxed experiences. OpenTable charges per-cover + monthly + a deposit fee; Tock/Resy require full migration. Deposits cut no-shows ~57% but operators can't afford the platform tax.
ideas.who: Sonoma's 425+ wineries and tasting rooms, fishing/kayak charters — Copper Bay's warm local channel.
ideas.gap: The generic restaurant deposit widget is already done well (Carbonara, Resmio, Tablein). Survives only as the winery/charter niche sold through Copper Bay's local relationships.
ideas.buildPlan: Static reserve page + Stripe Checkout deposit + Resend/Twilio reminders, embeddable as a <script>. 3-day Vercel build.
needsOwner: FORGE Stripe Connect platform account (white-label/reseller tier)
ideas.notes: PARKED 2026-06-08 under the widened-scope mandate: distribution depends entirely on the owner's private local channel, which no longer counts as reach. Revivable if the owner specifically wants a local play.

ideas.title: Marina Slip Waitlist & Day-Use Lite
ideas.oneliner: A lightweight public waitlist plus day-use launch reservation page with deposit collection for small marinas and county boat launches.
ideas.problem: Most small marinas run on spreadsheets; Dockwa/DockMaster ($99-500/mo) are built for full-service marinas. County launches still mail PDF forms.
ideas.who: Sub-50-slip marinas, county park boat launches, yacht clubs, kayak/SUP outfitters.
ideas.gap: Snag-A-Slip is a marketplace, not a self-hosted widget; the big suites are over-built. Nothing affordable serves only waitlist + day-use for the smallest operators.
ideas.buildPlan: Calendar + form + Stripe deposit + Resend confirmation. 3-4 day Vercel build. Dog-food at Lake Sonoma Marina first.
ideas.notes: PARKED 2026-06-08 under widened scope. NOTE: most defensible of the parked set — complements the owner's existing marina-booking SaaS and has a real seed client (Lake Sonoma). Revive first if the owner wants a local one.

ideas.title: Job-Completion Report + Review Push
ideas.oneliner: Tech snaps before/after photos and the customer gets a branded PDF of what was done plus a one-tap Google-review CTA while the goodwill is fresh.
ideas.problem: CompanyCam is photo-only; ServiceTitan/Jobber bury photos inside expensive suites. Nobody owns the customer-facing 'completion moment'.
ideas.who: Roofers, painters, HVAC, plumbers — Copper Bay's trades base.
ideas.gap: Photo apps are internal-facing; suites treat photos as secondary; none close the customer-facing review loop with a branded completion report.
ideas.buildPlan: PWA camera + Cloudinary upload + client-side PDF + public report URL + Google-review deep link. 3-4 weeks (iOS Safari camera/upload is non-trivial).
ideas.notes: PARKED 2026-06-08 under widened scope (trades/local channel + heaviest build). Revivable as part of a Copper Bay trades stack.

ideas.title: Local GEO Audit (agency lead magnet)
ideas.oneliner: Enter a business name and location to get a report card on AI-Overview citation, LocalBusiness JSON-LD validity, and NAP consistency.
ideas.problem: AI Overviews hit ~25.8% of US searches and local businesses fear being invisible to AI search. Paid GEO tools are generalist and $49-199/mo.
ideas.who: Local businesses worried about AI-search visibility, and the agency that pitches them.
ideas.gap: Free AI-visibility checkers are already crowding; the zero-secret slice is an agency distribution asset, not a product.
ideas.buildPlan: Static explainer + client-side JSON-LD/schema validator + NAP check + 'book a GEO audit' CTA. 1-2 days.
needsOwner: SerpAPI/Serper (only for the live AI-Overview citation tier later)
ideas.notes: PARKED 2026-06-08: below threshold AND always an agency lead-magnet rather than a standalone product. Belongs to Copper Bay marketing, not the Labs portfolio.

ideas.title: Review-Pulse (white-label add-on)
ideas.oneliner: A QR/link micro-app that routes happy customers to a Google review and unhappy ones to private feedback — sold as a configured, agency-branded add-on.
ideas.problem: Birdeye starts $299/mo and Podium $249-599 — priced for franchises, locking out solo operators who still want more Google reviews.
ideas.who: Single-location local businesses already on Copper Bay's roster.
ideas.gap: The cheap standalone lane is saturated (WiserReview, Reputigo, OpenWidget, NiceJob) and the experience-gate pattern is a standard feature, not a differentiator.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page + Google Maps review deep-link + sentiment fork; no API keys for MVP. 1-2 days.
ideas.notes: PARKED 2026-06-08: below threshold and too crowded to win as a standalone. Only viable bundled into a Copper Bay trades stack.

ideas.title: Contractor Instant-Quote Page (agency-install)
ideas.oneliner: A done-for-you, pre-configured ballpark-estimate page for a trade vertical that qualifies inbound leads before the phone call.
ideas.problem: Trades waste ~15 min/call on 'how much for X?' tire-kickers. Field-service suites force the whole business onto a platform when the pain is one narrow page.
ideas.who: Plumbers, HVAC, landscapers, electricians, painters — Copper Bay's core trades client base.
ideas.gap: Generic DIY quote-widget builders already exist and are free. The reshape to a consumer cost-estimator had no real distribution edge or moat.
ideas.buildPlan: JSON-driven question tree -> ballpark range -> lead email via Resend. 2-day build.
ideas.notes: KILLED by owner 2026-06-08. Teardown DONE — GitHub Pages disabled and repo archived/read-only (full hard-delete pending; PAT lacks delete_repo scope). No defensible distribution loop or moat. Do not revisit as a standalone product.
